newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. AFRICAN OIL INDUSTRY URGED TO RESOLVE DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: S. AFRICAN OIL INDUSTRY URGED TO RESOLVE DISPUTE.

text.p: Auditor-General Henri Kleuver on Monday called for urgent action by the South African Department of Minerals and Energy to resolve the long-standing dispute between the oil industry and oil from gas producer Mossgas.
The dispute, dating back to 1994, centres on the fact that the oil industry has been buying synthetic fuel from Mossgas at prices lower than the industry receives for its own fuel.
The aim was to compensate the oil industry for having to take on extra fuel, at times forcing it to export some of its own production.

To compensate Mossgas for the lower prices received, it has been paid subsidies totalling some 523.2 million rand from the equalisation fund, which is funded from fuel levies. But Mossgas now wants the oil industry to pay it the In-Bond-Landed-Cost (IBLC) prices that the industry itself receives.
In a special report, Kleuver said he doubted whether this arrangement was in the best interests of the taxpayer and motorist.
"It is recommended that the department, as a matter of urgency, considers new ways and means of securing a resolution of the apparant impasse between Mossgas and industry," he said.

South African Petroleum Industry Association (Sapia) director Colin McClelland told Reuters that the industry had bought Mossgas output since the plant went onstream in 1992 "although there was no statutory obligation or commercial gain for them to do so".
The industry had, however, wanted compensation in terms of lower prices for Mossgas fuel as it would have to export its own excess capacity at lower prices to accommodate Mossgas.
Since mid-1996, when it started becoming a marginal importer of gasoline, the industry had offered to pay import parity prices for Mossgas petrol, but had received no response.
"If Mossgas really feels aggrieved, it should take us to court, but we believe we have fully met the agreement originally made," McClelland said.

He questioned the inference made in the report that the oil industry had benefited from the arrangement, saying that it had bought and sold Mossgas fuel at the same price and had done this even though it had no legal obgligation to do so.
Kleuver said that he was concerned that there had been no formal agreement between the industry and Mossgas on pricing since 1994.
